Take A Dog Out For The Day

Borrow a dog that needs the exercise and take it hiking - good for the dog, good for you, free for everyone.

Cost
Free / Under £20pp
Time
Half-day
People
Solo / Duo, Small Group (3-6)
Where
Park / Outdoor, Community Org
Bring
Nothing in particular

Why this matters

Dogs that spend long stretches in kennels get measurably stressed, and that stress makes them harder to rehome - a loop that's hard to break. Meanwhile plenty of owners are ill, working long shifts or temporarily unable to walk their dog and have nobody to ask. Both problems are solved by someone who was going for a walk anyway.

How to do it

There are two versions of this, and both are useful.

Helping an owner: pet owners often need someone to look after their dog for a day, or just take them out for exercise when they can't. Illness, a hospital appointment, a brutal work week. Websites like BorrowMyDoggy connect owners with people who want to spend time with a dog, and you arrange walks or short-term sitting between yourselves.

Helping a shelter: some shelters run "dog for a day" programmes and need a brief screening first. These are rarer than people assume - most shelters focus on medium-term fostering rather than day trips. But almost all of them need regular dog walkers, which reduces kennel stress and improves a dog's chances of being adopted.

If you're already planning a hike, a trip to a park or a day in the woods, this costs you nothing extra.

Practical notes: - Be honest about your experience. A reactive or anxious dog is not a beginner's dog. - Ask about recall, triggers, and whether they can be off-lead before you go anywhere open. - Bring water and a bowl, and check the route works for the dog's age and fitness. Not every dog wants a 15km hike.
